# bpy catalog lanes

A lane makes a group of pieces as `catalog/blender/<lane>/` scripts, writing GLBs and `entries.json` to
`catalog/data/extra/bpy-<lane>/`. Blender 5.2, headless:
`blender -b --factory-startup --python catalog/blender/<lane>/build.py -- [slug ...]`.
Convention: metres, Z up, piece front faces **-Y** (export turns it into glTF +Z, the editor's front).

## Modules (import read-only; do not edit the shared ones, add your own `parts.py`)
- `kit.py`: `reset`, `box`, `cylinder`, `taper_leg`, `lathe`, `cushion`, `curve_tube`, `material`, `finish`,
  `export(path)` -> `{size_m, tris, bytes}`. `at` is the bottom centre (top centre for fabric).
- `kit_shapes.py`: real geometry where a texture reads flat.
  `reeded_panel(w, h, depth, at, spec, reed_w=0.02)` (vertical half-round reeds on the -Y face, flat back),
  `fluted_cylinder(r, h, at, spec, flutes=24, reeded=False, radius_top=None)`,
  `cane_panel(w, h, at, tint=)`, `alpha_material(spec, tint)`, `shrink_images(512)`.
- `kit_cloth.py`: curtains. `pair(width, drop, at, spec, tint, heading="pinch"|"wave", open_fraction=0.35)`,
  `drape(...)` for one panel (`side` = where it stacks), `rod(length, at, spec, rings=0)`.
  Every row keeps the full fabric width (fullness x width), so opening a panel deepens its folds; noise makes
  folds uneven, the hem flares and kicks forward. ~13k tris per 1 m x 2.6 m panel. `sim_frames=25` adds a
  Blender cloth pass (about 1.7 s per panel, 27 Sep 2026, M-series Mac): it only softens the hem a little, so it is off by default.
- Do not send fabric through `kit.finish`: its cube projection smears the weave across folds. `kit_cloth`
  writes UVs by arc length itself.

## Materials (`catalog/materials/<id>/`, format in its README)
Specs: a folder id, or `paint:#hex`, `ceramic:#hex`, `metal:#hex`, `glass`, `mirror`. `tint="#hex"` multiplies
the tint-ready grey. New on 27 Sep (`catalog/tools/import_cc0_more.py`):
- `oak-rift` straight grain, 1.0 m tile, default colour pinned to `oak`'s. Use it for legs, rails, slats and
  any small part. `oak` (flat-cut cathedrals, 1.83 m tile) looks swirly and marbled on small parts.
- `teak`, `terrazzo` (grey chips: tint-ready drops chroma, so coloured-chip terrazzo is not possible).
- `cane`: procedural 8-way Breuer cane with `opacity.jpg` (`"alpha": true`). `kit.material` ignores the
  opacity map, so use `kit_shapes.cane_panel` or `alpha_material`. That path exports alphaMode MASK as one RGBA PNG and
  still works under `kit.export`'s JPEG setting.
- For whoever next edits kit.py: when `material.json` has `"alpha": true`, `kit.material` should wire `opacity.jpg`
  (Non-Color) -> Math GREATER_THAN 0.5 -> BSDF Alpha and set `surface_render_method = "DITHERED"`, which is what
  `alpha_material` does now.
- No distinct CC0 rift ash exists. `ash-light` (Poly Haven ash_veneer) is already straight-grained.

## entries.json (one object per piece)
`slug, name, kind, colors[], price_amd (int), materials[], style, tags[], source_url: "generated:bpy",
license: "CC0 (generated by varpet)", notes, placement, glb, size_m [w, d, h], mesh_extents_m`.
**`placement` is required: `floor` | `wall` | `surface`.** Search drops extra furniture that has no placement.

**Glass:** kit's `glass` (transmission + alpha 0.25) previews as grey haze. For drinkware and display glass use a near-white
base, alpha ~0.2, no transmission, thick bottoms (see catalog/blender/homebar/); check the GLB keeps alpha blend.

**Fixture kinds (toilet, sink, fridge, stove, tv, radiator, kitchen_* ...) are hidden when the slug or notes contain
`wall`, `mount`, `hang` or `lift` anywhere, even inside a word ("changing", "lifted").** Only wall_art, mirror, clock and
wall_hanging may say "Wall-hung". Bed-kind names must contain "bed" and avoid foundation, box spring, folding, guest bed,
cot, slats, rollaway (the designer drops those as bare bases).

## Kinds the editor places
- Editor kinds: sofa chair table bed cabinet lamp rug shelf decor wall_art mirror.
- Subtypes mapped by `catalog/select_editor_set.py` EDITOR_KIND_OF: desk -> table; dresser, wardrobe, nightstand -> cabinet;
  stool, ottoman, bench -> chair; vase candle sculpture books cushion throw_blanket basket tray bowl lantern
  picture_frame toy planter mattress pet_bed -> decor; clock, wall_hanging -> wall_art; crib -> bed;
  changing_table -> dresser; blind -> curtain; towel_rack -> shelf.
- Also placeable as extras (`catalog/search.py` EXTRA_FURNITURE_KINDS, NATIVE_EXTRA_KINDS): curtain, blind,
  toilet sink bathtub shower fridge stove oven washing_machine dryer dishwasher microwave tv monitor computer
  laptop speaker printer game_console kitchen_cabinet kitchen_counter kitchen_island radiator fan coat_rack
  shoe_rack plant. Check both files on main before choosing a new kind.

## Budget
< 60k tris and < 3 MB per GLB. Each 1k textured finish costs ~0.7 MB. With more than 3 finishes, call
`kit_shapes.shrink_images()` before `kit.export`.

## Look-and-fix loop
1. Build, then render: `blender -b --python catalog/render_previews_studio.py -- <glb dir> <png dir>`. It is a drop-in for
   `render_previews.py`: same CLI and naming. It adds AgX, a studio backdrop, reflections and a whole-bbox fit.
   It skips PNGs that already exist, so delete them to re-render.
2. Put the PNGs on a contact sheet (PIL) and look at it: grain scale, swirl, floating parts, sideways
   meshes, clipped whites, cropped tops.
3. Fix, rebuild only that slug, re-render, look again. Stop when the sheet reads as the real product.
Reference: `catalog/data/previews-extra/toolkit-before-after.png`.
